Key indicators for turbofan engine degradation (based on C-MAPSS dataset knowledge):
- **Healthy engines**: Lower temperatures (T24, T30, T50), higher pressures (P30, Ps30), higher core speeds, lower fuel flow ratios, higher bypass ratios, higher coolant bleeds. Sensor values are relatively stable with small slopes.
- **Degrading engines**: Moderate increases in temperatures, moderate decreases in pressures and speeds, moderate slopes indicating trend.
- **Critical engines**: Significantly elevated temperatures (especially T50, T30), significantly reduced pressures (P30), reduced core speeds, increased fuel flow ratios, steeper slopes indicating rapid degradation.

- NRc (Corrected core speed): Healthy ~8130-8145

- W32 (LPT coolant): Healthy ~23.3-23.4, Degrading ~23.1-23.3, Critical ~<23.1
